ANGARA IN THE BOARD OF REGENTS -WESTERN MINDANAO STATE UNIVERSITY Dear Maybr Lobregat: This has ieference to your query on the matter of your designation as representative of Hon. Juan Edgardo M. Angara in the Board of Regents, Western Mindanao State Universitv, particularly on the issue of WHETHER SAID DESIGNATION VIOLATES SECTION 7, ARTICLE IX(B) OF THE 1987 CONSTITUTION and SECTION 94 OF RA 7160, ORITHE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991. As by virtue of a letter dated 31 August 2010, you were appoj_teda designated. and authorized by Hon. Juan Edgardo M. Angara as the latter's true and awful re r entative, and to sit in all the regular and/or special meetings of the Board of rustees of the Western Mindanao State University (BOR-WMSU) where Mr. Angara Sits as Chairman of the Committee on Technical and Higher Education. Further, tpe appointment, designation, and authorization granted in your favor was not permanent and neither was it absolute, considering that in the same aforesaid letter, Mr. Angara provided for the limitations of such representation — that you cannot gelegate the appointment and authority granted without Mr. Angara's written consent, and that your authority does not preclude Mr. Angara's prerogative to attend future regular and/or special board meetings of the BOR- WMSU which necessitate the latter's attendance and participation. You wrote this Office in view of the issues being raised by Alumni Regent, Mahmor N. Edding of the BOR-WMSU who wrote to Mr. Angara on 24 January 2011, requesting that the our appointment be recalled or withdrawn on the ground that the such appointm nt or designation is violative of Section 7, Article IX-B of the 1987 Constituti n and Article 94 of RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government code oft e 1992 (LGC). Section 7 bf the 1987 Constitution states that : Section 7. No elective official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no appointive official shall hold any other office or employment in the Government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof including Government- owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries. -2- Section 94 of the LGC provides: SECTION 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidates Who Lost in Election. - (a) No elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position no elective or appointive local official shall hold any other office or employment in the government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries. Acting on your query, we are of the view that your appointment does not violate Section 7, Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution and Article 94 of RA 7160. A car ful reading of the appointment letter from Mr. Angara dated 31 August 2010 show d that the such appointment, designation, and authorization is in the nature of a me e REPRESENTATION or AGENCY, and not the appointment and designation whic the law prohibits against elective officials. The asis for agency is representation, that is, the agent acts for and on behalf of the incipal on matters within the scope of his authority and said acts have the same legal effect as if they were personally executed by the principal. On the part of the p incipal, there must be an actual intention to appoint or an intention naturally infer inten is ge G.R. Absent such mutual intent, there erally no agency. (Yun Kwan Byung vs. Philippine Amusement Gaming Corporation, . 163553, December 11, 2009) 1 August 2010 appointment letter clearly spelled out your authority - your entation is limited to physically representing Mr. Angara in any régular or I meetings of the BOR-WSMU. The authority to represent Mr. Angara is not permanent considering that the latter can revoke or withdraw the authority at n pleasure. Finally, during the subsistence of said authority, Mr. Angara may, sole and exclusive discretion, attend and participate in these special and r meetings of the BOR-WSMU, notwithstanding your appointment. ove-quoted, Section 7 of Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution disqualifies e officials from being appointed or designated to any public office in whatever ity. Of material significance in the application of this constitutional provision is oper construction to be given to the words "appointment" and "designation." er, the words "appointment" and "designation" have well-defined significations "Appointment" is commonly understood as the selection, by the rity vested with the power, of an individual who is to exercise the ions of a given office. When completed, usually with its confirmation, the intment results in security of tenure for the person chosen unless he is eable at pleasure because of the nature of his office. On the other hand, nation" imports the imposition of additional duties, upon a person already in ublic service by virtue of an earlier appointment or election. A mere nation" does not confer upon the designee security of tenure in the position or which he occupies in an "acting" capacity only. (Binamira vs. Garrucho, 188 SCRA 158; Sevilla vs. Court of Appeals, 209 SCRA 637, emphasis supplied) Appl ing these principles to the instant case, the representation granted and auth rized by Mr. Angara does not confer any power or right to you when you sit as a representative in the BOR-WSMU special or regular meetings. Neither is there any nction to be exercised when you sit as Mr. Angara's representative in the said Boar for the simple reason that Mr. Angara REMAINS to be the official holder of said position in the BOR-WSMU, and not you.

-3- Ergo, the prohibition set forth under Section 7, Article XI of the 1987 Constitution and Article 94 of the LGC do not apply in your case. However, you shall receive no additional compensation while acting as representative of Mr. Angara in the BOR-WSMU special and regular meeting Warmest regards, JE M.
